name: University of California, Berkeley
description: Birthplace of RISC-V. Home of the Rocket Chip and BOOM processors; Patterson and Waterman developed the ISA here.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
description: Integrates RISC-V into computation structures and secure hardware research. Custom RTL via Bluespec.

name: Stanford University
description: Deep specialization in digital system design and hardware/software interface coursework using RISC-V.

name: Carnegie Mellon University
description: Rigorous RISC-V architectures applied to verified, high-assurance embedded and dependable processor design.

name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
description: Computer Organization and Design courses use RISC-V pipelines for hands-on processor prototyping and RTL labs.

name: University of Pennsylvania
description: CIS 5710 students design custom RV32IM cores from scratch, bridging software layers to silicon.

name: University of Nevada, Las Vegas
description: International champion of the RVfpga training initiative, providing architecture lab blueprints worldwide.

name: Arizona State University
description: Open-standard ISAs as a cornerstone of senior-level FPGA-based system integration and secure microelectronics.

name: University of Texas at Arlington
description: CSE 4372 cohorts synthesize and test custom multi-stage RISC-V processors deployed to FPGA hardware.

name: Portland State University
description: Official RISC-V International Academic Partner advancing SoC verification pedagogy.

name: University of Michigan
description: EECS 470 labs teach out-of-order CPU microarchitecture with custom RISC-V processor design.

name: Rice University
description: RVR Lab implements specialized RISC-V microcontrollers scaling up to multi-width vector computing cores.

name: University of Pittsburgh
description: High-performance computing design with fault-tolerant, resilient execution architectures in open hardware.

name: Penn State University
description: Integrating resilient RISC-V variants into space-grade, radiation-hardened satellite computing.

name: Purdue University
description: Open hardware verification, SoC methodologies, and modern system constraints embedded in core engineering.

name: Georgia Institute of Technology
description: Pioneering many-core cluster research and custom RISC-V domain-specific AI hardware accelerators.

name: University of California, San Diego
description: Hardware-security education and side-channel evaluation using RISC-V infrastructure.

name: University of Washington
description: VLSI physical design and instruction pipeline optimization taught via open-standard ISA frameworks.

name: Cornell University
description: CS 3410 teaches system software interaction with hardware through custom RISC-V implementations.

name: Tufts University
description: Foundational assembly, compilation targets, and machine-level computing fundamentals over native RV32I.

name: University of California, Santa Cruz
description: Champions open-source hardware engineering built around scalable RISC-V academic specifications.

name: Harvey Mudd College
description: Major academic hub for RISC-V development, driven by Prof. David Harris — co-author of 'Digital Design and Computer Architecture: RISC-V Edition.' Students build full-featured, open-source RISC-V microprocessors and SoCs from the ground up.

name: Miami University
description: ECE lab-based RISC-V coursework with embedded systems integration.

name: ETH Zürich
description: Origin of PULP Platform: CVA6, Ibex, and Snitch. Luca Benini's IIS lab is Europe's anchor for open-source RISC-V silicon with multiple tapeouts including MLEM at IHP 130nm.

name: University of Bologna
description: Co-originator of PULP Platform with ETH Zurich. PULP cluster architecture; graduate courses use RISC-V. GAP8 spun out of joint research. Active in space-grade and 5G NTN RISC-V research.

name: Barcelona Supercomputing Center / UPC
description: Europe's strongest RISC-V safety-critical program. Home of NOEL-V and Sargantana. Dr. Kosmidis holds RISC-V Educator of the Year (2019). Active in EU post-quantum cryptography standards.

name: University of Cambridge
description: Home of CHERI-RISC-V. Cambridge is authoring and validating the RVY (CHERI) capability extension to the RISC-V ISA, with formal golden models and fuzz testing infrastructure.

name: Technical University of Munich
description: Prof. Georg Sigl's group has produced three RISC-V ASICs for post-quantum cryptography in 65nm and GlobalFoundries 22nm.

name: Politecnico di Torino
description: Most concentrated PQC ISA extension work in Europe. Three papers at RISC-V Europe 2026 covering CIRCE, HORCRUX, and CHIMERA. ML-KEM 22nm ASIC delivering 139x speedup over software. Active fault injection and side-channel research.

name: CEA (French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission)
description: France's primary RISC-V research institution. Flying V radiation-hardened cache, fault-tolerant CVA6, ANSSI ECC accelerator, and ALPES SoC platform targeting AI, space, and automotive silicon.

name: EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne)
description: Co-developer of X-HEEP, an open-source RISC-V SoC platform designed to lower the barrier to chip design for research and education. First silicon confirmed via Croc/MLEM tapeout at IHP 130nm. Joint research with ETH Zurich and European RISC-V institutions.

name: Politecnico di Milano
description: ECE research programs with RISC-V silicon emulation and embedded architecture coursework.

name: Chalmers University of Technology
description: Computer architecture research with RISC-V emulation and FPGA-based coursework.

name: Czech Technical University in Prague
description: Faculty of Electrical Engineering architecture research with RISC-V emulation and embedded silicon projects.

name: RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau
description: Prof. Wolfgang Kunz's EDA group published on transient-execution side-channel detection in out-of-order RISC-V cores (SonicBOOM). Participant in Scale4Edge national RISC-V edge computing program.

name: University of Bremen / DFKI
description: Muhammad Hassan (DFKI / University of Bremen) presented formal verification work on RISC-V at RISC-V Europe 2023. Prof. Rolf Drechsler's group has published on RISC-V verification and computer architecture.

name: Forschungszentrum Jülich
description: HPC research center with RISC-V vector (RVV) work. Stepan Nassyr presented automated BLIS kernel generation for RISC-V RVV at RISC-V Europe 2023 as part of the EUPILOT HPC project.

name: IHP Microelectronics (Leibniz Institute)
description: Junchao Chen and Li Lu presented two RISC-V papers at RISC-V Europe 2023 including the TETRISC resilient quad-core RISC-V SoC. Also operates the open IHP 130nm PDK used for European academic RISC-V tapeouts.

name: University of Rennes / IRISA / INRIA
description: Prof. Angeliki Kritikakou presented dual-core lockstep RISC-V using HLS for real-time safety-critical systems at RISC-V Europe 2023. Graduate computer architecture and embedded systems research.

name: Université Bretagne Sud
description: William Pensec (PhD) presented DIFT-protected RISC-V cores against fault injection attacks at RISC-V Europe 2023. Lab-STICC ARCAD team research in hardware security.

name: Mines Saint-Étienne (IMT)
description: Joint research with CEA Leti on RISC-V security; PhD students co-supervised on trace encoder security topics. Microelectronics and computer science engineering programs with RISC-V security research.

name: Université Grenoble Alpes / TIMA Lab
description: Arthur Perais (TIMA Lab) conducts high-performance processor microarchitecture research targeting RISC-V. CEA/UGA joint research environment in Grenoble, a major European semiconductor hub.

name: École Normale Supérieure Paris-Saclay
description: Graduate computer science research with RISC-V components. Presenter at RISC-V Europe 2023.

name: University of Manchester
description: Juan Fumero (APT Research Group) presented TornadoVM hardware acceleration on RISC-V at RISC-V Europe 2023. Advanced Processor Technologies group has documented RISC-V work and participates in the AERO project.

name: University of Edinburgh / EPCC
description: Nick Brown (EPCC) presented HPC work on RISC-V at RISC-V Europe 2023. EPCC is the UK's leading HPC research center with RISC-V in emerging architecture evaluation.

name: Universidad de Cantabria
description: Jaime Palacios (MSc) presented 'Towards a RISC-V Educational HW Lab' at RISC-V Europe 2023 — documenting active curriculum development for hardware-centric RISC-V courses in CS/Engineering degrees.

name: IMSE-CNM / Universidad de Sevilla
description: Luis Felipe Rojas Muñoz (PostDoc) presented Root-of-Trust components for RISC-V SoCs using RO-PUF/TRNG at RISC-V Europe 2023. Joint CSIC/Universidad de Sevilla hardware security research.

name: Universitat Politècnica de València
description: Enrique S. Quintana-Ortí (UPV) presented TinyML matrix multiplication on multicore RISC-V (GAP8) at RISC-V Europe 2023. Parallel Architectures Group active in RISC-V HPC and embedded computing.

name: Universidad de Málaga
description: Computer architecture research with RISC-V elements. Represented at RISC-V Europe 2023.

name: Sapienza University of Rome
description: Marcello Barbirotta (PhD) presented Dynamic Triple Modular Redundancy on RISC-V microarchitecture at RISC-V Europe 2023. Hardware fault tolerance research group with RISC-V coursework integration.

name: University of Pisa
description: Daniele Rossi presented HW-SW Interface for RAS (Reliability, Availability, Serviceability) in RISC-V architectures at RISC-V Europe 2023. Digital systems and reliability research.

name: University of Torino
description: Iacopo Colonnelli presented distributed workflow systems on RISC-V HPC platforms at RISC-V Europe 2023. CS department involvement in RISC-V HPC research.

name: KU Leuven / imec-DistriNet
description: Marton Bognar (imec-DistriNet) presented hardware security work on RISC-V at RISC-V Europe 2023. Prof. Frank Piessens's security group. imec's industrial connections create strong applied RISC-V exposure.

name: University of Twente
description: Gerard Rauwerda presented SmallSat RISC-V payload platform at RISC-V Europe 2023. ECE and CS programs have computer architecture research relevant to RISC-V, including space computing applications.

name: Johannes Kepler University Linz
description: Lucas Klemmer (JKU PhD) presented a DSL for visualizing RISC-V pipelines at RISC-V Europe 2023. Institute for Complex Systems research in RISC-V tooling, verification, and waveform analysis.

name: TU Wien (Vienna University of Technology)
description: Philipp Tomsich (VRULL GmbH / former TU Wien; RISC-V Board Treasurer and TSC Vice-Chair) has deep compiler and runtime systems expertise linked to this institution. TU Wien Informatics and ECE programs have computer architecture and compiler research aligned with RISC-V toolchain development.

name: Universidade do Minho
description: Prof. Sandro Pinto presented the CROSSCON IoT security stack with RISC-V at RISC-V Europe 2023. Centro ALGORITMI/LASI group has documented RISC-V embedded security research.

name: University of Athens
description: Prof. Dimitris Gizopoulos co-leads the Vitamin-V Horizon Europe project delivering a production-grade open-source RISC-V cloud ecosystem (OpenStack, Kubernetes, QEMU, gem5). His group extended Cache Timing Vulnerability Scoring to RISC-V.

name: ICS-FORTH
description: Manolis Marazakis leads the RISER Horizon Europe project building first-generation all-European RISC-V cloud server and accelerator prototypes, integrating EPAC1.5 RISC-V vector processors into standalone compute nodes.

name: University of Tirana
description: First Western Balkans institution with an explicit national strategy for RISC-V adoption. Kushtrim Shala (Digital Valley Albania / EU EDIH) presented Albania's RISC-V education strategy at RISC-V Europe 2025.

name: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (ICT/CAS)
description: Home of XiangShan — the highest-performance open-source RISC-V processor globally. 28nm and 14nm tapeouts completed. Origin of the 一生一芯 (One Life One Chip) national student tapeout program.

name: Zhejiang University
description: Geographic anchor of China's RISC-V cluster. Joint research with Alibaba T-Head (XuanTie C906/C910 cores, Uncore PMU). 一生一芯 national tapeout program participant.

name: Tsinghua University
description: China's top university. Patterson & Hennessy RISC-V Edition is the primary architecture textbook. Faculty publish in processor microarchitecture, hardware security, and compiler backend research.

name: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
description: CS359 Computer Architecture and graduate courses use RISC-V. Active in national CPU design competitions. Research covers RISC-V accelerators, vector extensions, and FPGA prototyping.

name: Peking University
description: Adopted RISC-V as instructional ISA. Institute of Software contributes to open-source RISC-V toolchain development. Active in national CPU design competitions.

name: University of Science and Technology of China
description: RISC-V pipeline implementation in Computer Organization courses. Winner of national CPU design competitions. 一生一芯 program participant.

name: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
description: Strong processor design culture. Participates in the 一生一芯 (One Life One Chip) national RISC-V tapeout program. Public lab materials include RISC-V pipeline design exercises.

name: Southeast University
description: School of Electronic Science and Engineering is one of China's strongest microelectronics programs. RISC-V processor design appears in digital IC design and computer architecture courses. Active in Nanjing's semiconductor design cluster.

name: National University of Defense Technology
description: China's premier military-academic institution. Graduate courses use RISC-V as a design target for high-performance and reliable computing. NUDT's influence on national computing standards gives its RISC-V research outsized policy relevance.

name: Fudan University
description: School of Microelectronics is one of China's strongest IC design programs. RISC-V appears in graduate chip design coursework and student tapeout projects. Located in Shanghai's semiconductor design hub.

name: Nanjing University
description: Department of Computer Science and Technology has adopted RISC-V in computer organization courses and participates in the 一生一芯 (One Life One Chip) national student tapeout program.

name: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
description: China's most electronics-specialized university. RISC-V appears in digital systems, computer architecture, and SoC design coursework. Located in Chengdu, a growing chip design hub in Southwest China.

name: Harbin Institute of Technology
description: Top engineering university in Northeast China. School of Computer Science and Technology has computer architecture research referencing RISC-V; student teams participate in national RISC-V processor design competitions.

name: Beihang University
description: Aerospace and defense-oriented engineering university. Computer architecture and embedded systems courses reference RISC-V; faculty research in fault-tolerant and real-time systems aligns with RISC-V's open verification properties.

name: Xi'an Jiaotong University
description: Strong ECE programs with computer architecture coursework that has adopted RISC-V edition materials. Research in energy-efficient computing references RISC-V implementations.

name: Sun Yat-sen University
description: Flagship university of South China. CS and ECE programs include computer architecture content with RISC-V. Located in the Pearl River Delta semiconductor region near Huawei headquarters in Shenzhen.

name: South China University of Technology
description: Strong engineering programs in South China. ECE and CS architecture courses tracking the RISC-V textbook transition; faculty research in embedded IoT and SoC design references RISC-V.

name: Wuhan University
description: CS and ECE programs with computer architecture coursework. Located alongside HUST, China's strongest RISC-V institution in Wuhan, creating cross-institutional RISC-V research influence.

name: Beijing Institute of Technology
description: Defense-adjacent engineering university with strong ECE programs. Computer architecture and embedded systems courses reference RISC-V; focus on safety-critical systems aligns with RISC-V's verifiable open ISA.

name: ISCAS / PLCT Lab (Chinese Academy of Sciences)
description: PLCT Lab (Programming Language and Compiler Technology) at Institute of Software, CAS is China's most important RISC-V toolchain contributor — maintaining and extending GCC, LLVM, QEMU, and open-source RISC-V tools nationally.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Madras
description: Home of the SHAKTI processor program — multiple production RISC-V silicon tapeouts from a student/faculty team. Funded by MeitY. NPTEL computer architecture courses use RISC-V and reach millions nationally.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay
description: CS 683 Advanced Computer Architecture uses RISC-V. NPTEL contributions in computer architecture reach millions nationally.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur
description: One of the first IITs to formally adopt Patterson & Hennessy RISC-V Edition as the primary architecture textbook. Research includes processor design and compiler backend work.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
description: COL216 and COL718 use RISC-V for pipeline design, hazard analysis, and lab assignments. Public course materials available.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur
description: Original IIT. NPTEL computer organization courses produced here use RISC-V and reach millions of students nationally.

name: Indian Institute of Science
description: India's premier research university. Graduate architecture courses use RISC-V. Hardware security and VLSI research output with strong industry connections to Bangalore's semiconductor cluster.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad
description: Active computer architecture research group with published RISC-V based accelerator and custom ISA extension work. Computer Architecture coursework uses RISC-V; faculty have contributed to open-source RISC-V toolchain work.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee
description: ECE and CS programs include computer architecture sequences that have moved toward RISC-V as the Patterson & Hennessy RISC-V edition became the standard IIT textbook. Faculty research in embedded systems and digital design.

name: Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi
description: Electronics Engineering department with computer architecture coursework tracking the national IIT curriculum alignment toward RISC-V. Research output in VLSI design supports adoption.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati
description: CS and ECE programs at Northeast India's flagship technical institution. Computer architecture faculty have published in processor design; RISC-V integration follows IIT-wide textbook trends.

name: IIIT Hyderabad
description: Center for VLSI and Embedded Systems Technology (CVEST) has produced RISC-V related publications and student projects. Graduate architecture courses reference RISC-V implementations.

name: BITS Pilani
description: India's top private technical university. Strong undergraduate research culture has produced RISC-V processor implementations and FPGA projects documented on GitHub across the Pilani, Goa, and Hyderabad campuses.

name: NIT Tiruchirappalli
description: Consistently ranked the top NIT. ECE department computer architecture courses have adopted RISC-V edition textbooks; faculty research in embedded systems and VLSI supports active adoption.

name: NIT Calicut
description: Strong ECE/CS programs in Kerala; computer architecture instruction has moved toward RISC-V. Kerala's active open-source technology culture reinforces adoption.

name: IIIT Bangalore
description: Research-focused IIIT with industry ties to Bangalore's chip design ecosystem. Graduate programs in VLSI, embedded systems, and computer architecture reference RISC-V; student capstone projects include RISC-V core implementations.

name: Jadavpur University
description: One of India's oldest and most respected state engineering universities. ECE and CS departments have research groups in VLSI and digital design tracking RISC-V through national textbook shifts.

name: Anna University
description: Apex technical university for Tamil Nadu, affiliating hundreds of engineering colleges. Given proximity to IIT Madras and the SHAKTI ecosystem, RISC-V exposure is documented through affiliated faculty collaboration.

name: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS)
description: Strongest documented RISC-V program in Latin America. GAPH group publishes RISC-V microarchitecture and NoC research. Computer Architecture courses use RISC-V as the primary ISA reference.

name: Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP)
description: Brazil's top research university for engineering. MC722 Computer Architecture uses RISC-V. Accelerator and memory hierarchy research. Industry connections to Campinas semiconductor cluster.

name: Universidade de São Paulo (USP)
description: Brazil's largest university. Escola Politécnica courses have adopted RISC-V. International RISC-V keynote presence at RISC-V Europe Summit 2025.

name: Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica (ITA)
description: Brazil's most selective engineering institution. RISC-V in safety-critical and aerospace embedded systems coursework. Graduates enter Embraer, AEB (Brazilian Space Agency), and defense electronics.

name: Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG)
description: Department of Computer Science has research groups in computer architecture and embedded systems. RISC-V appears in graduate-level architecture coursework and student thesis projects.

name: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro / COPPE
description: COPPE is Brazil's most prominent graduate engineering school. Processor architecture research has RISC-V-referenced publications; undergraduate architecture courses have tracked the MIPS-to-RISC-V textbook transition.

name: Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (UFPE)
description: Centro de Informática (CIn) is one of Brazil's most research-active CS departments in embedded systems and hardware design. Faculty and student projects have produced RISC-V aligned work.

name: Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC)
description: Strong ECE and CS programs with embedded systems research. Computer architecture courses have adopted RISC-V edition textbooks; faculty in digital systems and SoC design have published relevant work.

name: Universidade de Brasília (UnB)
description: Federal capital university with CS and ECE programs. Computer architecture sequence has moved toward RISC-V; proximity to government ICT policy creates alignment with Brazil's semiconductor and open-hardware priorities.

name: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM)
description: Latin America's largest university. Facultad de Ingeniería and IIMAS have computer architecture content with RISC-V appearing in graduate research and select advanced undergraduate courses.

name: CINVESTAV
description: Mexico's premier public research and graduate institution. CS and Electrical Engineering departments have produced RISC-V and open-ISA research publications. CINVESTAV Guadalajara has documented embedded systems RISC-V output.

name: Tecnológico de Monterrey (ITESM)
description: Mexico's leading private technical university with nationwide campuses. Computer Engineering and CS programs have adopted RISC-V edition architecture textbooks; strong industry-connected lab culture supports FPGA-based RISC-V projects.

name: Instituto Politécnico Nacional (IPN)
description: Large public polytechnic with ESIME engineering schools across Mexico. Computer architecture sequences have tracked the MIPS-to-RISC-V transition; IPN's scale means adoption reaches a large engineering student population.

name: Universidad de Chile
description: Chile's top public university. Department of Computer Science (DCC) has computer architecture courses with RISC-V content. Faculty research includes processor design and systems programming referencing RISC-V.

name: Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile
description: Chile's highest-ranked university. Strong CS and ECE programs; computer organization and architecture courses have adopted RISC-V edition materials. Faculty research has produced relevant open-ISA output.

name: Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María
description: Chile's most engineering-focused university with a strong FPGA lab culture. RISC-V appears in digital systems, computer architecture, and capstone project contexts — a natural fit for hardware implementation courses.

name: Universidad de los Andes
description: Colombia's top-ranked private university. Electrical/Electronic and Systems/Computing Engineering departments have produced architecture-related research. Computer organization courses have moved toward RISC-V.

name: Universidad Nacional de Colombia
description: Colombia's flagship public university. Engineering and CS programs at Bogotá and Medellín campuses include computer architecture sequences with RISC-V content in course materials and graduate research.

name: Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA)
description: Departamento de Computación within Exactas is Argentina's strongest CS department. Arquitectura del Computador courses have tracked the RISC-V textbook transition; faculty research in systems and architecture includes RISC-V references.

name: Universidad Nacional de La Plata (UNLP)
description: Strong CS and engineering programs. Facultad de Informática has computer architecture content; research groups in digital systems and embedded computing have produced RISC-V aligned work at the graduate level.

name: Instituto Tecnológico de Buenos Aires (ITBA)
description: Argentina's most selective private technical university. Computer architecture courses use RISC-V; capstone project culture has produced student RISC-V processor implementations.

name: University of the Philippines Diliman
description: Most likely Philippine institution with documented RISC-V exposure through architecture research and open-ISA coursework. Microelectronics and Microprocessors Lab with ECE and CS programs.

name: De La Salle University
description: Strong ECE and CS programs; embedded systems and computer organization courses make this a natural candidate for RISC-V integration. DLSU has industry-connected labs tracking open ISA trends.

name: Mapúa University
description: Engineering-focused institution with ECE and CE programs. Practical, lab-intensive culture aligns well with RISC-V FPGA integration and hands-on architecture coursework.

name: Mindanao State University – Iligan Institute of Technology
description: The strongest engineering school in Mindanao and the most likely Philippine regional institution to achieve Tier 1 status. ECE and CS programs are research-active; DOST-ERDT network membership accelerates open-ISA adoption.

name: University of San Carlos
description: One of the oldest and most research-active private universities in the Visayas with strong ECE and CE programs. Research culture makes it a likely early adopter of RISC-V hardware instruction.

name: CMKL University
description: Thailand-based research university with a focus on engineering and technology. Faculty have participated in RISC-V International events, representing Southeast Asia's growing engagement with open-ISA hardware education.

name: University of Genova
description: Faculty researchers have presented RISC-V work at international conferences. DITEN and DIBRIS departments conduct embedded systems and digital architecture research aligned with RISC-V.

name: Munich University of Applied Sciences (Hochschule München)
description: Prof. Stefan Wallentowitz is a prominent RISC-V ecosystem figure and educator based here, contributing to open-source RISC-V tooling and teaching. Distinct from TU Munich; strong applied engineering focus with active RISC-V curriculum development.

name: Inatel (Instituto Nacional de Telecomunicações)
description: Brazil's national telecommunications technology institute. Faculty have participated in RISC-V International events; embedded systems and communications hardware programs make it a natural fit for open-ISA adoption in Brazil's growing semiconductor ecosystem.

name: University of Genova
description: Active RISC-V research presence with representation in the RISC-V International Academia & Training SIG. Computer engineering and electronics research programs with RISC-V integration.

name: Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM)
description: Formal research partnership with StarFive Technology includes donation of RISC-V educational development boards directly to the School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering for active coursework integration.

name: Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM)
description: Published research documenting use of RISC-V processors in Computer Architecture and Microprocessor & Microcontroller courses as a direct replacement for outdated ISA models. One of Malaysia's clearest cases of formal RISC-V curriculum adoption.

name: Advanced Semiconductor Academy of Malaysia (ASEM)
description: Professional semiconductor training program in Cyberjaya operating the Global Semiconductor Exchange Program (GSEP). Curriculum includes intensive RISC-V computer architecture, assembly programming, and processor SoC design. Not a degree-granting institution but a key node in Malaysia's RISC-V workforce pipeline.
